title: JASSM/LRASM production support, capacity investment, and integration testing precede delivered inventory
source_unit: Official DoD and Lockheed Martin production-support, capacity, and flight-test records
geography: United States defense-industrial and integration-test records

contract_value.unit: nominal US dollars; announced IDIQ value

scope.value: system upgrades, integration, production, sustainment, management, and logistics support for JASSM/LRASM and variants

observations.method: Official DoD contract announcement, retrieved through a text proxy after direct HTTP 403; scope and value are retained as announced, without converting an IDIQ ceiling/support contract into production output.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not provide awarded task-order obligations, accepted quantities, delivery, fielding, or inventory; expected completion is a schedule, not realization.
observations.subgroup: JASSM and LRASM production-support contract and variants.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad support vehicle can carry engineering, sustainment, and logistics work without being a production-quantity record.

capacity_action.value: large-lot procurement/capacity expansion for JASSM and LRASM

facility.value: 225,000-square-foot intelligent factory brought online in 2022 alongside existing production facilities

observations.method: Official Lockheed Martin account of JASSM/LRASM ramp-up and capacity investment; company-reported capacity language is kept separate from government acceptance and delivery records.
observations.uncertainty: Company account does not state actual line rate, utilization, unit output, variant allocation, or accepted/delivered quantity.
observations.subgroup: JASSM/LRASM production system and capacity investment.
observations.counterinterpretation: A new or automated facility can improve potential throughput while bottlenecks remain in inputs, testing, certification, workforce, or downstream acceptance.

milestone.value: first phase of F-35C LRASM flight-science program completed

observations.method: Official Lockheed Martin release describing the completed first phase and test window; integration testing is treated as a technical realization stage distinct from production acceptance and fielding.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not provide accepted missile quantities, operational availability, inventory location, delivery, or maintenance capacity.
observations.subgroup: LRASM F-35C flight-science integration; JASSM appears as part of the AGM-158 test-asset context.
observations.counterinterpretation: A successful flight-science phase may validate integration while the broader system remains in test, production, or certification stages.

related_sources.claim: The earlier cross-source finding separates procurement, production plans, integration tests, delivery, and leverage.
Supplier locations have capability context but not specific work-package assignment.
Poland's JASSM-ER delivered-quantity and acceptance arrow remains open.
Persists the extracted DoD announcement fields and proxy-retrieval boundary.

boundary: These records establish production-support commitment, capacity investment, and an integration-test milestone. They do not establish accepted production, customer delivery, fielding, maintenance, replaceability, or geopolitical leverage.
